name: Election Results
author: rpierce99
description: Live election results: a scrolling ticker of important races plus a full-screen interrupt when a race is newly called. Auto-activates for your state's primary + general (dormant otherwise), drains stale calls from the ticker, and survives restarts. Filterable to your state. NYT baseline provider + optional California SoS county/city rollup.

versions.changelog: Render text 1-bit (no anti-aliasing) so glyphs stay crisp on the LED grid

versions.notes: Rebuild the ticker when something else clears its scroll cache. _display_ticker() gated on its own _scroll_ready flag, which Vegas cannot clear when it invalidates the cached scroll image, so the mode could yield an empty frame while still holding race data.
changes: Fixed the bundled test_mode fixtures failing to load on Windows, which left every panel blank.
Documented the twelve remaining settings and replaced the placeholder screenshot with real renders of both display modes.

versions.notes: Rebuild the ticker when something else clears its scroll cache. _display_ticker() gated on its own _scroll_ready flag, which Vegas cannot clear when it invalidates the cached scroll image, so the mode could yield an empty frame while still holding race data.
Add a GPL-3.0 LICENSE file (project-standard license; this plugin previously shipped without one).
Apply config changes live via on_config_change (state, filters, providers, scroll speed); rebuilds providers and the race store and re-fetches so edits take effect without a display restart.

Rename the internal data_model module to election_data_model so it can't collide with another plugin's identically-named module. The loader puts plugin modules on sys.path by bare name; a deferred import (providers/__init__) could otherwise bind a different plugin's data_model and fail to load.

Fix the called-race interrupt looping forever: give colliding local races (e.g. multiple 'Mayor' races) a stable id derived from NYT's per-race id instead of an order-dependent counter, so the newly-called diff no longer re-fires every fetch.
